public_rationale: The reliability study supports a serious underlying concern: capability improvements had not produced equally strong reliability gains. It does not establish that most products fail what they actually promise. The customer report supplies a limited positive counterpoint, but not independent proof. The searched evidence lacks the product-by-product comparison needed to judge as sold and for the most part. It also does not establish the passage's causal explanation for the visibility of achievements.
limitations: Benchmark model configurations and marketed products are different populations.
Advertisements may promise bounded assistance rather than dependable unrestricted autonomy.
The causal clause is not resolved by the observational performance evidence.
Post-period product comparisons were not applied retrospectively.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI agents as sold do not exist and are, for the most part, fundamentally broken.

statement.excerpt: AI agents do not, as sold, actually exist. Every “AI agent” you read about is a chatbot talking to another chatbot connected to an API and a system of record, and the reason that you haven’t heard about their incredible achievements is because AI agents are, for the most part, fundamentally broken.

from_speaker: AI agents do not, as sold, actually exist.
a chatbot talking to another chatbot connected to an API and a system of record
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that most marketed agents materially fail to deliver their advertised autonomous capabilities.
As sold requires matching actual product promises to tested behavior, including any stated limits or need for supervision.
For the most part concerns prevalence among marketed systems. It is not interchangeable with the percentage of difficult benchmark tasks that fail.
The chatbot description is treated as an architectural assertion, not proof that the resulting system cannot work.
Use January through March 2026, the latest completed quarter before the post, because the ongoing observation names no reporting period.
The passage also offers a causal explanation for a supposed lack of public achievements. Neither that absence nor its cause is established by a capability benchmark.
criteria.support_condition: A reasonably representative comparison of marketed products and their contemporaneous promises shows that most materially fail to deliver their advertised autonomous functions under the stated operating conditions.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A reasonably representative comparison shows that most deliver their advertised functions under the stated conditions. Individual successes challenge an absolute nonexistence reading but cannot establish the market-wide majority.
